privacy.description: What My Gift Lockers collects, why, and the choices you have.
privacy.intro: My Gift Lockers (“we”, “us”) helps you keep the sizes, dates and wishes of the people you love in one place, and run gift exchanges. This policy explains what we collect on mygiftlockers.com and in our apps, how we use it, and the choices you have. We don’t sell your information and we don’t show ads.

items.account: Account details. If you sign in, your email address. If you sign in with Google, we also receive your name and profile picture from Google. We never see your Google password.
items.locker: What you put in your locker. Names, relationships, clothing and shoe sizes, birthdays and anniversaries, mailing addresses, favorites and notes for you and the people you add, including children you manage as a parent or guardian.
items.profile: Your own profile and connections. If you save your own profile, it’s copied to the lockers of the people you choose to connect with, limited to the parts you choose to share.
items.exchanges: Gift exchanges. The exchange name, date, budget and message; each participant’s name, optional email and wishlist; exclusions; and who drew whom.
items.invites: Invites. When someone fills in an invite you sent, the details they choose to share with you.
items.technical: Technical data. Our hosting provider keeps standard server logs (such as IP address, browser type and request time) to run and secure the service. We remember your language choice in a cookie. We don’t use advertising or analytics trackers.
items.photos: Photos and gift ideas. Photos you add to a card (up to 5, adults only) and the card’s details, including your private notes, are used to suggest gifts. They’re stored privately in your account.
items.payments: Payment app handles. If someone adds where they take money gifts (for example a Venmo username or a Zelle email), it’s stored on their card. People only see it when that person chooses to share it; it’s never shown in gift exchanges or used for gift ideas.

use.title: How we use it

items.service: To provide the service: show your locker, run exchanges, draw names and reveal matches.
items.signIn: To sign you in and keep your account secure.
items.reminders: To email you reminders before birthdays, anniversaries and holidays in your locker. Every reminder has a link to stop them.
items.contact: To respond when you contact us.
items.ai: To suggest gifts: when you ask for gift ideas, the card’s details, your notes and its photos are sent to Anthropic’s Claude model (through Anthropic’s API, or Amazon Bedrock) to generate the list. Neither uses them to train models.

use.noSale: We don’t sell or rent personal information, and we don’t use it for advertising.

items.locker: Your locker is private to you (and to co-guardians you add for a child’s profile).
items.exchange: Exchange participants can see the exchange details and, after names are drawn, only their own match and that person’s wishlist, through their private link. Organizers can manage participants and may view assignments.
items.connections: People you connect your profile with see the parts you share, until you change that or disconnect.
items.links: Anyone holding a private exchange or invite link can use it, so share links only with the people they’re meant for.
items.affiliate: Shop links may be affiliate links (for example Amazon Associates), which can earn us a commission at no cost to you. The store sees that you came from us, not who the gift is for.

providers.title: Service providers
providers.body: We store and process data with Amazon Web Services (hosting, sign-in and database, in the United States). If you choose Google sign-in, Google processes that sign-in under its own privacy policy. Invites you send by text, email, WhatsApp or other apps go through those apps, not through us. Example photos on gift ideas load from Unsplash, which sees your browser’s request like any website.

google.title: Google user data
google.body: With Google sign-in we request only your basic profile (name, email address and profile picture) to create and identify your account. We don’t access Gmail, Contacts, Drive or any other Google data, and we don’t share Google user data with anyone except as needed to run the service. Our use of information received from Google APIs adheres to the <link>Google API Services User Data Policy</link>, including the Limited Use requirements.

children.title: Children
children.body: My Gift Lockers is meant for adults. Parents and guardians may add their children’s sizes and dates to their own locker; children don’t create accounts. If you believe a child has given us personal information directly, contact us and we’ll delete it.

keeping.title: Keeping and deleting your data
keeping.body: We keep your information while your account is active. You can edit or delete profiles and exchanges at any time, and you can delete your account and everything in it yourself, right away: on the website under My locker → Delete account, or in the app under Settings. You can also email us and we’ll do it within 30 days, apart from anything we must keep by law.

security.title: Security
security.body: Data is encrypted in transit (HTTPS) and at rest with our hosting provider, and access is limited to what each person is allowed to see. No system is perfectly secure, but we work to protect your information.

changes.title: Changes
changes.body: If we make material changes, we’ll update this page and the date above, and tell signed-in users in the app.

privacy.translation: This policy is translated for convenience; if versions differ, the English version applies.

free.a: Yes. Creating an exchange, inviting people and drawing names costs nothing.

accounts.a: Only the organizer signs in. Everyone else joins from the invite link and adds their wishes, with no account or app needed.

secret.q: Can the organizer see who got whom?
secret.a: Matches stay hidden, so the organizer can play too. If something needs fixing, the organizer can choose to peek or redo the draw.

exclusions.q: Can I stop couples from drawing each other?
exclusions.a: Yes. Add exclusions before you draw, for couples, housemates or anyone who shouldn't get each other.

budget.q: Can we set a spending limit?
budget.a: Yes. Set a budget when you create the exchange, and everyone sees it when they join.

apart.q: Does it work if we're not in the same place?
apart.a: Yes. Everyone joins from a link on their phone or computer, and each person gets a private link showing who they're buying for and that person's wishes.

kids.a: Yes. The organizer can add people by name, such as a child they'll help, so everyone is included.

circle.a: Usually names are drawn at random. With one big circle, the draw makes a single loop through everyone, so you can open gifts in turn and each gift leads to the next person.

hub.title: International size charts
hub.metaTitle: Size Conversion Charts: Shoes, Clothing & Rings
hub.metaDescription: Free size conversion charts for shoes, clothing and rings: US, UK, EU, Japan, Brazil, Mexico and Colombia sizes side by side. Find the right size for a gift.
hub.intro: Buying a gift for someone who shops in another country's sizes? These charts put US, UK, European, Japanese, Brazilian, Mexican and Colombian sizes side by side.

shoes.blurb: Men's, women's and kids' shoes in 7 sizing systems.
shoes.title: Shoe size conversion chart
shoes.metaTitle: Shoe Size Conversion Chart: US, UK, EU, Japan, Brazil, Mexico
shoes.metaDescription: Convert men's, women's and kids' shoe sizes between US, UK, EU, Japan (cm), Brazil, Mexico and Colombia.
shoes.intro: Find a shoe size in any of seven sizing systems. Start from the US size in the first column and read across.
shoes.cmNote: Japan and Mexico label shoes by foot length in centimeters.
shoes.kidsNote: US toddler and little kid sizes 4 to 13.
shoes.tip: Heel-to-toe foot length in centimeters is the one shoe measurement that converts reliably everywhere. Measure standing up, then compare it with the brand's own chart.

clothing.blurb: Dresses, tops and pants, including letter sizes.
clothing.title: Clothing size conversion chart
clothing.metaTitle: Clothing Size Conversion Chart: Dresses, Tops & Pants
clothing.metaDescription: Convert women's dress sizes, letter sizes for tops and men's pant sizes between US, UK, EU, Japan, Brazil, Mexico and Colombia.
clothing.intro: Clothing sizes change from country to country. Use these charts to turn a US size into the size printed on labels elsewhere.
clothing.womensNote: US numeric sizes, with the matching letter size.
clothing.topsNote: Brazil and Mexico use their own letters, and Japanese sizes run about one size smaller.
clothing.pantsNote: US men's pants are labeled waist × inseam in inches, for example 32×30. This table converts the waist.
clothing.tipTitle: Tip: when in doubt, size up
clothing.tip: A gift that's slightly big can still be worn, and most stores exchange sizes. It also helps to know whether they like a slim, regular or relaxed fit.

rings.blurb: US, UK, EU and more, with inside diameter.
rings.title: Ring size chart
rings.metaTitle: Ring Size Conversion Chart: US, UK, EU, Japan & mm
rings.metaDescription: Convert ring sizes between US, UK letters, EU, Japan, Brazil, Mexico and Colombia, with inside diameter and circumference in millimeters.
rings.intro: Ring sizes are the hardest to guess. Find a size in any system, plus the inside diameter in millimeters.
rings.note: EU sizes are the inside circumference in millimeters.
rings.tipTitle: Tip: measure a ring they already wear
rings.tip: Measure the inside diameter of a ring that fits the same finger and find the closest match in the last column. Fingers swell when warm, so ring sizes are best measured at the end of the day.
